faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

When you see a headline about the **latrell mitchell salary**, it’s easy to forget that most Australians are paid by the hour. Whether you’re a full‑time employee, a casual worker, or negotiating a new role, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure helps you compare offers and plan your budget. This article walks through the standard formula, explains casual loading and superannuation, and shows how the National Minimum Wage and award rates fit in.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full‑time employees, the standard is 38 hours per week (the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act). If you work a different pattern, adjust the hours accordingly. For example:

- $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 = $59,280 per year
- $50 per hour × 38 hours × 52 = $98,800 per year

This formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It’s a starting point, not a precise determination.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours), according to the Fair Work Ombudsman. This rate applies to employees who are not covered by an award or registered agreement. Most workers, however, are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimums for their industry or role. Award rates also include penalty rates for weekends, nights, and public holidays.

If you’re unsure which award applies, use the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or the Modern Awards Pay Database from the Fair Work Commission.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. This loading is applied before any annual conversion. For example:

- Base rate: $26.44 per hour
- Casual rate: $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour
- Annual casual pay: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80

When using a calculator, never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter your base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this in more detail.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the National Minimum Wage:

- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

For a casual on $33.05 per hour, the fortnightly gross is $2,511.80 (38 hours × 2 weeks).

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not come out of your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year (2026–27). So if your annual ordinary earnings are $80,000, your employer must contribute $9,600 to your super fund. This is separate from your take‑home pay. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax Considerations

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Tax Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents (2026–27):

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The tax‑free threshold and Medicare reduction thresholds are based on the latest available figures. For a precise estimate, use the [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

### Putting It All Together: The Latrell Mitchell Salary Context

While the **latrell mitchell salary** is a high‑profile figure in Australian sport, the same conversion principles apply. If his reported annual salary is, say, $1.2 million, that implies an hourly rate of roughly $607 (based on 38 hours × 52 weeks). Of course, professional athletes have different contract structures, but the math is the same. For most workers, the focus is on the minimum standards set by the Fair Work Commission and the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. Remember: super is shown as an employer contribution on top, not deducted from your pay.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Assume 38 hours for full‑time.
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by the employer.
- The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour.
- Award rates may be higher – check your award.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take‑home pay.

For more details, visit the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for comparisons with ABS data.

*Disclaimer: Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.*
